newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel mulls selling bank stakes on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Israel mulls selling bank stakes on bourse.

text.p: The government company in charge of privatising Israel's banks is considering selling controlling stakes in the banks on stock exchanges in Tel Aviv and abroad, government sources said on Thursday.
The plan was put together by Ze'ev Abeles, supervisor of banks at the central bank, who is seeking to rekindle the moribund bank privatisation programme.

M.I. Holdings, the state company in charge of bank privatisations, has already said it plans a secondary offering for 10 percent of Bank Leumi probably in the first quarter of 1997. Israel Discount Bank is preparing a prospectus based on its results for the first nine months of 1996 and will probably be floated in February.

The central bank, however, prefers to first sell off controlling stakes of at least 20 percent in the banks to strategic investors. Now Abeles is willing to sell stakes of 15 or even 12 percent, the government sources said.

Under Abeles' plan, instead of the central bank exclusively seeking a strategic investor group, it would allow such a group to organise through the stock market. The group could then buy a controlling stake as long as it met with Bank of Israel approval.

A plan to offer shares in United Mizrahi Bank earlier this year failed and Edmond Safra, the sole bidder in a tender for a controlling stake in Leumi, Israel's second-largest bank, dropped out last year.
Bank Hapoalim is being tendered now, but of the two bidders that emerged one has already dropped out and the second has yet to win Bank of Israel approval to make a formal bid.
